question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the minimum corpus requirement that each scheme of an AIF (other than a Social Impact Fund) must maintain?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 10(c) / Regulation 12(1)(b): each scheme of an AIF must have a minimum corpus of INR 20 crore. Social Impact Funds are a carve-out at INR 5 crore; Special Situation Funds require INR 100 crore. The INR 20 crore minimum must also be met at First Close date. **The Trap:** INR 100 crore is the SSF floor; INR 50 crore is a common distractor (confused with FPI/QIB thresholds); INR 10 crore is not prescribed. Social Impact funds at INR 5 crore is a deliberate exception many candidates miss. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests this as a product-availability rule. XIX-C adds the sub-category exceptions (SIF INR 5 cr, SSF INR 100 cr). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: If an open-ended Cat III's corpus falls below INR 20 crore due to redemptions, the fund must notify SEBI within 2 days of the triggering redemption and restore the corpus within 3 months — failing which it must compulsorily redeem all investors. Build a Liquidity Ratchet clause into the PPM.
